question.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x$ is 

$$
\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}+\sqrt{{(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m})}^{2}+1}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}+\sqrt{\frac{16-8{m}^{2}+{m}^{4}}{16{m}^{2}}+1}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}+\sqrt{\frac{16+8{m}^{2}+{m}^{4}}{16{m}^{2}}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}+\sqrt{{(\frac{{m}^{2}+4}{4m})}^{2}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}+|\frac{{m}^{2}+4}{4m}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $m>0,$ we have $\frac{{m}^{2}+4}{4m}>0,$ and we can remove the absolute value in the above expression. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4-{m}^{2}}{4m}+\frac{{m}^{2}+4}{4m}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{m}).\end{aligned}
$$
